added.summary: Every component document under the engine package's src/ui/components/ (its group directories included) is built in: a game's document uses one by the name its <meta name="component"> declares (<StatBar/>, <AbilityBar/>) without copying it. The cook bundles each built-in component the game's documents reach, with its string tables and the files it names, under the reserved id @ui/<path under src/ui> (@ui/components/stat-bar.svelte), as it bundles a look's @styles/; two built-in documents of one name fail the cook. A game document declaring the same component name (what og ui eject writes) wins, and the engine's copy is then not bundled. og ui types reads the built-in components' props and events for the documents that use them.

Every screen document under the engine package's src/ui/screens/ is built in as well: og.load.document(world, "@ui/screens/pause.svelte") loads it without a copy and og.ui.push(world, "pause") shows it, as with a game's own screen. The cook bundles each built-in screen whose id the game's code names as a string literal, with its strings and the components it uses. A game document declaring the same screen name (what og ui eject writes) wins: the engine's is not bundled, and loading its @ui/ id loads the game's copy at ui/<file> instead.

Loading a document also loads every component document it uses, and theirs, once each: the game's own component of a name, else the built-in one. A screen needs only its own og.load.document call; loading a component explicitly as well is harmless. og dev's reload loads a component an edit starts using.
An ejected component replaces the built-in one of its name and loads with the screens that use it; the message no longer asks for a separate og.load.document.
